summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and recent DVT/PE on anticoagulation was admitted for bilateral lower extremity pain and severe calf cramping. Evaluation revealed stable clot burden on ultrasound with partial clearance in the greater saphenous vein and no new DVT. Ankle X-rays showed no fractures or avascular necrosis. The pain was attributed to a combination of radicular nerve symptoms from prior back surgery and possible joint-related discomfort. He was managed with gabapentin for neuropathic pain, acetaminophen, and PRN opioids. His chronic conditions remained stable, and he was discharged home with instructions to hold warfarin on the day of discharge, restart the next day, follow up with primary care and podiatry, and monitor weight for signs of fluid retention.
problems: Pain in joint, ankle and foot
Acute venous embolism and thrombosis of deep vessels of proximal lower extremity
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
